rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (60 trials, all off_track, score 50.60, down from 75.97 in iteration 1). Cutting base_speed 1.4 to 1.2 and kd 0.2 to 0.1 changed the results in two different ways. Progress fell sharply: s-bend 0.29 to 0.155, oval 0.16 to 0.10, slalom 0.115 unchanged. max_error did not improve, staying at 0.061 to 0.064 on every track. Line losses on the s-bend fell from 1.95 to 1.0, but the slalom stayed at 2.0. Steering oscillation fell as predicted: s-bend 0.23 to 0.14, slalom 0.14 to 0.14, oval 0.11 to 0.08. The lower kd did reduce jitter, but the lower speed cost most of the progress and did not move the failure point. The Evaluator's rule for progress falling with no reduction in max_error therefore applies: return base_speed toward 1.4 and keep kd at 0.1. The Evaluator's rule for oscillation below about 0.15 with max_error near 0.06 also applies (s-bend 0.14, slalom 0.14), so kp should rise in one modest step from 2.0 to 2.5. Changes: base_speed 1.2 to 1.4 (restores the progress that iteration 1 reached); kd stays at 0.1 (keeps the lower jitter); kp 2.0 to 2.5 (the one-step increase the Evaluator specified, aimed at pulling max_error below 0.06). Geometry, weights, ki and line_loss are unchanged so the kp effect can be read directly. Expected result: progress near iteration 1 levels (s-bend about 0.29, oval about 0.16), steering_oscillation at or below about 0.15, and max_error falling from about 0.062 toward or below 0.06 on the oval and slalom. Hypotheses to test: (H1) the bend failure is driven by insufficient steering authority rather than speed, so kp 2.5 should reduce max_error and line losses; (H2) kd 0.1 keeps oscillation below 0.15 at speed 1.4; (H3) if oscillation rises above 0.15 with kp 2.5, the next step is kd 0.05 rather than further kp. Measurements wanted: max_error and its location on each track, line_loss_events per track (especially the slalom, which stayed at 2.0), steering_oscillation, progress per track, and completion_time if any run finishes.
